# Mechanical Engineer - Integration & Test — Figure

---

**Job ID:** Not listed (Greenhouse posting id `4672013006`)
**Date Posted:** Not listed
**Date Applied:** Aug 8, 2026
**Salary Range:** $120,000 – $175,000

---

## Job Summary

Supports Figure's test infrastructure team, designing and building prototype hardware across the integration and test organization. North San Jose, CA, 5 days/week in-office.

---

## What You'll Do

- Design and build prototype robot components, validating hardware against real-world loading and failure conditions.
- Own prototype integration and test equipment cradle-to-grave; develop dynos for actuator testing, validation, and integration.
- Generate accurate 2D drawings using GD&T per ASME Y14.5 for tight tolerances and proper fits.
- Collaborate with mechanical engineering and systems-integration teams on hands-on testing.

### Required Qualifications
- 2+ years of experience in mechanical engineering
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical, Biomechanical, Robotics, Mechatronics, or similar
- Experience using 3D CAD software to design parts with complex geometry
- Experience designing and building prototypes; ability to write/maintain clean design-process documentation

Bonus: CATIA V6, manufacturing-process/first-article-inspection familiarity, actuator experience (strain-wave/planetary/cycloidal), sensor/motor/electromechanical-systems exposure, FEA/simulation or Python/MATLAB programming.

### Education
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical, Biomechanical, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a similar field.

### Benefits
Total compensation may include additional components/benefits depending on the role; details shared if an offer is extended.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Aug 8, 2026

- **Very strong overlap, likely overqualified for the listed level:** the 2+ year bar is comfortably exceeded (~6 years of professional experience), the degree matches directly, and prototype hardware design/build/validation is extensive — the linear-motor platform work alone (converting servo-driven ballscrews to a linear-motor architecture, validated at 4-micron precision and 4 m/s with a 30 kg payload) is functionally equivalent to "developing dynos for actuator testing, validation, and integration."
- Electromechanical systems, sensors, and motors are deep matches (multi-sensor Modbus data acquisition at high frequency, custom AC heaters and dual-voltage electrical design), and both **Python and MATLAB** are explicit skills — a direct hit on the FEA/simulation/programming bonus qualification.
- **Minor gap:** no CATIA V6 specifically (general CATIA is listed); no strain-wave/planetary/cycloidal actuator terminology by name, though precision motion-system design experience is closely adjacent.

### Now — Aug 22, 2026

No material change — the skills list hasn't shifted since Aug 8, 2026, and this remains a strong, likely overqualified match at the stated level.
